sentences.text: Westphaliasaurus was an extinct plesiosaur, a marine reptile estimated to reach a length of about 4.5 meters.
Amateur paleontologist Sönke Simonsen found the fossils in 2007 in the Höxter district near Bielefeld, Germany. Leonie Schwermann and Martin Sander formally named the genus in 2011.
The known remains include a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that lacks the skull and approximately 38% of the upper neck vertebrae.
Taxonomically, Westphaliasaurus belongs to the family Plesiosauridae.
This animal lived during the Lower Jurassic, specifically the Pliensbachian stage, between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago in Westphalia, northwestern Germany.
